# PostGIS

> > PostGIS is a spatial database extender for PostgreSQL, enabling geographic object support and location queries with industry-standard SQL.

PostGIS adds geospatial capabilities to PostgreSQL through geometry/geography types, spatial indexing (GiST/R-Tree), and coordinate transformation. The project is maintained by OSGeo and integrates with tools like OpenStreetMap, osm2pgsql, QGIS, and Safe FME.

## Key Topics

- PostGIS
- PostgreSQL
- spatial-queries

- [How do I use spatial indexes? | PostGIS](https://postgis.net/documentation/faq/spatial-indexes): FAQ: creating & using GIST spatial indexes for query performance

- [PostGIS FAQ v3.3](https://postgis.net/docs/manual-3.3/PostGIS_FAQ.html): FAQ v3.3: coordinate reprojection, spatial storage, licensing info
- [PostGIS FAQ v3.2](https://postgis.net/docs/manual-3.2/PostGIS_FAQ.html): FAQ v3.2: geometry/geography types, spatial indexing, troubleshooting
- [PostGIS FAQ v3.0](https://postgis.net/docs/manual-3.0/PostGIS_FAQ.html): FAQ v3.0: spatial indexing, coordinate reprojection, version migration
- [PostGIS FAQ v2.5](https://postgis.net/docs/manual-2.5/PostGIS_FAQ.html): FAQ v2.5: spatial queries, licensing, compatibility with tools
- [PostGIS FAQ v2.2](https://postgis.net/docs/manual-2.2/PostGIS_FAQ.html): FAQ v2.2: materialized views, spatial queries, version migration
- [PostGIS FAQ v2.1](https://postgis.net/docs/manual-2.1/PostGIS_FAQ.html): FAQ v2.1: tutorials, troubleshooting, spatial queries, geometry/geography
